takeaways: Body text needs 4.5:1. Large text — 24px regular, or about 18.7px bold — needs 3:1.
Measure against the real background. Over gradients and photos, test the lightest spot behind the text.
Logos, purely decorative text and inactive (disabled) controls are exempt.
failures: Light gray helper, placeholder and caption text
White text on light brand colors — sky blue, yellow, orange
Text over photos with no overlay or scrim
check: Sample text and background with a contrast checker such as WebAIM or Stark.
Check every state: hover, pressed, selected, error.
For text on images, test the lightest area behind it.

quiz.question: A 16px regular label in #949494 sits on white — 3.03:1. Does it pass?
quiz.why: 16px regular isn’t “large text”, so 4.5:1 applies. #767676 is the lightest gray that passes on white — worth memorizing.

spec: Write the color pair and its measured ratio next to each text style.
Where text sits on an image, note the scrim or overlay it depends on.
List every state with its own pair: hover, pressed, selected, error.
review: Which pairs here were measured, and which were judged by eye?
What happens to this text in dark mode and in the error state?
Does anything look disabled that is actually active?
tradeoff: The brand color fails on white? Keep the hue for large type, fills and graphics, and choose a darker step for body text. An exception for one team becomes the standard for all.
system: Ship color tokens as approved pairs, not loose swatches. If a pair is not in the system, nobody has checked it.
pitch: Low-contrast text is one of the most common failures audits find, and the cheapest to fix once, in tokens.
